title: Command acknowledgement
description: DESCRIPTIVE, NOT NORMATIVE. Generated from firmware source at FW 1.8.0 and re-verified field by field against FW 2.1.4 (branch fix/2.1.4, release commit "chore(release): 2.1.4", whose parent is x-nearest-commit). x-source line numbers are from the 1.8.0 generation and are STALE; fields added or changed for 2.1.4 cite functions instead. This is not a specification and not a proposal; it records what the device emits today. Plane: D2C telemetry (acknowledging a C2D command). `required` lists only keys present in the minimal payload, i.e. those always emitted for this message type.

schema.description: Wire-contract identifier. Constant; bump signals a breaking payload change. Range/enum: Fixed literal "eflostop.v2".

ts.description: Device wall-clock when the message was built. Never below 1704067200 on the wire. Since 2.1.4 an event built before the first clock sync is not destroyed: it is held in the offline buffer and replayed after the first connect, with ts rewritten to the time the event happened, worked out from the hub uptime (the synced clock minus the uptime elapsed since gateway.uptime_s) and written into the buffer as soon as the clock first syncs. A pre-sync event still unstamped when the hub restarts (a restart before the clock synced) is dropped at replay, because its time cannot be known. Up to 2.1.3 every pre-sync event was destroyed, so a leak raised before the first sync was lost. Units: seconds (Unix epoch, UTC). Range/enum: >= 1704067200 (2024-01-01T00:00:00Z).
ts.x-source: build_envelope() / publish_json() main/telemetry/telemetry_v2.c; stamping ob_prepare_replay_locked() main/offline_buffer/offline_buffer.c; threshold EPOCH_VALID_THRESHOLD_TELEM

id.description: Immutable hub id derived from the WiFi STA MAC in eFuse. Same string used as the DPS registration id and the MQTT client id. Range/enum: "GW-" + 12 uppercase hex.

short_id.description: Last 2 bytes of the STA MAC as 4 hex chars. Also the SoftAP SSID suffix (WiFi-Hub-XXXX) the installer matches during setup. Range/enum: 4 uppercase hex chars.

name.description: User-assigned hub name from twin desired hub_name or C2D set_hub_name. NOTE the opposite convention on the twin plane, where hub_name is always emitted as "". Range/enum: free text, max 31 chars (HUB_NAME_MAX_LEN). Presence: conditional: OMITTED when the stored name is empty.

fw.description: Hub firmware version, read at runtime from the ESP-IDF app descriptor (PROJECT_VER). Never a hardcoded string. Range/enum: "2.1.4" for this release (CMakeLists.txt:12); "0.0.0" if the descriptor is empty.

uptime_s.description: Seconds since boot from the monotonic esp_timer. On an offline-buffer replay this is the ORIGINAL build-time value, possibly from a previous boot. For an event held from before the first clock sync (2.1.4) it is the uptime the replay used to work out ts. Units: seconds. Range/enum: >= 0.

type.description: Envelope discriminator. Tells the backend which `data` shape to expect. Range/enum: enum: "lifecycle" | "snapshot" | "event".

event.description: Event discriminator inside data. The single most important routing key for the backend event log. Range/enum across the whole D2C plane, 16 values: online | valve_state_changed | leak_detected | leak_cleared | cmd_ack | auto_close | auto_close_blocked_override | auto_close_reenabled | rmleak_cleared | rmleak_auto_cleared | water_access_override_enabled | water_access_override_expired | device_offline | device_recovered | rules_engine | health_engine (valve_flood_detected / valve_flood_cleared were retired in 1.9.0). The enum below lists the values this message type carries. Presence: always in lifecycle and in every event shape; ABSENT in snapshot.

id.description: Echo of the inbound command's correlation id. Range/enum: free text, max 63 chars. Presence: OMITTED (NOT "") when the inbound command carried no correlation id.

cmd.description: Echo of the command name, taken verbatim from the inbound cmd field (so it may be an unrecognised name); "unknown" when an oversized message was dropped before its name could be read. Presence: always.

status.description: Did the command succeed. Range/enum: enum: ok | error. Presence: always (cmd_ack only).

code.description: The failing command's name (NOT an error code): the same value as data.cmd. Presence: whenever data.error is present.

detail.description: Human-readable, end-user-facing failure reason; the only real discriminator. The valve commands (2.1.4) send exactly: "No valve is set up for this hub." (no valve provisioned; valve_open, valve_close, valve_set_state), "Valve is locked after a leak (RMLEAK). Clear it with leak_reset first, or use override to open the valve during a leak." (open: the valve's RMLEAK latch is asserted, or, since 2.1.4, a leak incident is latched with no override window, even with the valve disconnected), "Valve battery critical (≤10 %): the valve will not open. Replace the batteries." (open, last real valve battery <= 10 %), "The valve command could not be queued. Try again." (queue full). The full list per command is in C2D_COMMANDS.md §6.1. Presence: whenever data.error is present.

error.description: Failure detail container. Presence: status error only (every refusal supplies a detail).

data.description: Type-specific payload container. Attached on creation and NULL-checked since 2.1.4: if data or the gateway object cannot be allocated, the ack is not published (logged "Message not built (event) - out of memory"). Up to 2.1.3 an allocation failure published an envelope with no data key. Presence: always.
